hypothesis: For episodic observed-assignment cache, increasing retained inactive-slot capacity from 0 to 4 to 9 can improve churn but may have diminishing or negative cost-effectiveness. At a fixed primary churn penalty, an intermediate capacity may outperform the full 9 slots.
freeze: All capacity levels, schedules, seeds, output metrics, cost weights and classification committed before first original science; no capacity increase beyond accepted prior upper bound and no post hoc threshold selection.
source: Exact Y030 keyed nonuniform 16-key/cell geometry and exact Y033 finite recurrence/constant additional shifts; seven active identities per episode, eight episodes per seed, radius-two matching; no future states or evaluator-only history available to policy.
costs: Fixed modeled cost per policy = matching recursive calls + cache writes + cache lookup attempts + churn*w with w=1,3,10; w=3 is preregistered primary. Track actual writes on eviction; zero-slot policy makes no writes.
metrics: For each cap and schedule: heldout per-seed churn, exact match count, cache occupancy/write/read parity, recursive calls, legal cached preferences, sham-minus-retained net modeled cost all weights, and cache maximum observed occupancy.
classification: For constant schedule at primary w3, INTERMEDIATE_OPTIMUM if cap4 aggregate savings>0 and exceeds cap9; FULL_CAP_OPTIMUM if cap9>cap4 and cap9 aggregate savings>0; otherwise NO_CAPACITY_GAIN. INVALID if independent Hall maxima, unique geometry signatures, unchanged source/seed or per-capacity parity checks fail. Publish recurrent secondary in full regardless.
claim_limit: Synthetic fixed-assignment cache resource tradeoff only; no direct evidence for learned developmental intelligence or broader transfer; no accepted-ref mutation.
